content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Declaration-Site and Use-Site Variance** as part of **Generics and Type-System Design**. `out` supports safe covariance for produced values, while `in` supports contravariance for consumed values; invariant types allow both directions. Use the subtopics—Variance in Class Declarations, Type Projections, Star Projections—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: `out` supports safe covariance for produced values, while `in` supports contravariance for consumed values; invariant types allow both directions.

items.title: Variance in Class Declarations
items.text: Variance in Class Declarations should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.
